sources.name: National Payment System Act 78 of 1998 (consolidated, SAFLII)

entries.subject: nps_act_commencement
entries.display: National Payment System Act 78 of 1998 commenced on 28 October 1998
entries.notes: Assented to 20 October 1998 and published in Government Gazette 19402 of 28 October 1998.

entries.subject: sarb_recognises_payment_system_management_body
entries.display: The SARB may recognise a payment system management body to organise and regulate members in the payment system
entries.quote: the Reserve Bank may recognise a payment system management body established with the object of organising, managing and regulating the participation of its members in the payment system

entries.subject: record_retention_period
entries.display: Payment system records must be kept for five years
entries.quote: must retain all records obtained by them during the course of the operation and administration of a payment or Reserve Bank settlement system for a period of five years from the date of each particular record

entries.subject: non_compliance_penalty
entries.display: Offences under ss 6(2), 6A(4) or 12(8) carry a fine up to R1 million and/or five years' imprisonment
entries.quote: is liable to a fine not exceeding R1 million, or to imprisonment for a period not exceeding five years, or to both such a fine and such imprisonment

entries.subject: directive_effective_date
entries.display: A SARB directive under s12(1) takes effect three months after issue
entries.quote: A directive issued in terms of subsection (1) takes effect three months after it has been issued or on such earlier date as may be determined by the Reserve Bank.
entries.notes: Section 12(9)(a); directives under s12(3) take effect immediately.

entries.subject: pasa_recognition_year
entries.display: PASA was founded in 1996 and recognised by the SARB as the payment system management body in 1999
entries.quote: Founded in 1996 and recognised as a payment system management body by the SARB in 1999, the Payments Association of South Africa (PASA) is a self-regulatory organisation that governs the national payment system through rules, agreements, and a robust legal framework.

entries.subject: pasa_current_psmb_status
entries.display: PASA is currently the recognised payment system management body
entries.quote: PASA is currently recognised as the PSMB by the SARB.
entries.notes: Undated page; captured 2026-11-02. Source page undated; effective date recorded as the 2026-11-02 capture date.

entries.subject: settlement_via_samos
entries.display: Transactions cleared through a PCH system operator settle at the SARB in SAMOS (RTGS)
entries.quote: Transactions cleared through the PSO are eventually settled at the SARB through the Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system called SAMOS (South African Multiple Options Settlement).
entries.notes: Undated page; captured 2026-11-02. Source page undated; effective date recorded as the 2026-11-02 capture date.

entries.subject: debicheck_go_live
entries.display: Authenticated Collections (DebiCheck) went live in August 2018
entries.quote: The AC/DebiCheck system went live in August 2018 and the existing authenticated early debit order and non-authenticated early debit order collection systems were discontinued on 1 November 2021.

entries.subject: aedo_naedo_discontinued
entries.display: AEDO and NAEDO collections were discontinued on 1 November 2021
entries.quote: The AC/DebiCheck system went live in August 2018 and the existing authenticated early debit order and non-authenticated early debit order collection systems were discontinued on 1 November 2021.

entries.subject: card_interchange_revision_date
entries.display: Current ATM and card interchange rates apply from 5 February 2026
entries.quote: The current ATM and Card Interchange rates as revised from 05 February 2026 is as follows
entries.notes: Interchange is determined by the SARB under the Interchange Determination Process launched in 2011.

entries.subject: number_of_payment_systems
entries.display: South Africa has more than 18 different payment systems
entries.quote: In South Africa, consumers and businesses have a choice of more than 18 different payment systems, ranging from low-value card transactions to high-value bond exchange payments.
entries.notes: Page undated; captured 2026-11-02. Source page undated; effective date recorded as the 2026-11-02 capture date.

notes: Statutory facts are quoted from the consolidated NPS Act 78 of 1998. Institutional facts (PASA recognition, SAMOS settlement, DebiCheck cut-over, interchange revision) come from PASA and SARB pages.
